target.title: fix(e2e): share ClawHub preflight timeout across fetch and body
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where QA Lab Crabline inbound injection and runtime-parity mock `/debug/requests` fetches could hang indefinitely. Both paths used `fetchWithSsrFGuard` without `timeoutMs` and then called bare `response.json()`, so a hung or never-finishing admin/mock endpoint could stall the suite forever.

## Why This Change Was Made

Copy the existing `suite-runtime-gateway` pattern: pass `timeoutMs: 15_000` into `fetchWithSsrFGuard` and read JSON through `readProviderJsonResponse` on both surfaces. Add a caller-path hang regression for runtime-parity capture and a focused Crabline inbound assertion that the production helper receives the timeout + bounded JSON reader.

## User Impact

No end-user product change. QA Lab / Crabline CI scenarios fail closed on hung inbound or mock debug endpoints instead of hanging the suite process.

## Evidence

- Changed: `extensions/qa-lab/src/crabline-transport.ts`, `extensions/qa-lab/src/crabline-inbound-bounds.test.ts`, `extensions/qa-lab/src/runtime-parity.ts`, `extensions/qa-lab/src/runtime-parity.test.ts`
- Production caller paths:
  - `postCrablineInbound` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard({ timeoutMs })` + `readProviderJsonResponse`
  - `captureRuntimeParityCell` → `loadRuntimeParityMockToolCalls` → same pattern

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

QA Lab Crabline inbound injection now fails closed on a hung/stalled admin-inbound endpoint instead of hanging the scenario forever, and completing bodies still parse through the bounded reader.

### Canonical reachability path

`postCrablineInbound` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard({ url: adminInboundUrl, timeoutMs: QA_LAB_CRABLINE_INBOUND_TIMEOUT_MS })` → `readProviderJsonResponse` (`extensions/qa-lab/src/crabline-transport.ts:202`).

### Real environment tested

Real HTTP transport: a local `node:http` admin-inbound server on `127.0.0.1` that returns `200` headers plus one JSON chunk (`{"update":`) and then never sends another chunk or ends the response. The production helper `qaLabCrablineInboundTesting.postCrablineInbound` (exported via `extensions/qa-lab/api.ts`) is driven against that live socket with a minimal adapter manifest pointing at the server (`policy: { allowPrivateNetwork: true }` allows loopback), Node v22.23.1.

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
# Real HTTP admin-inbound server returns headers + one chunk then stalls; drive
# the production postCrablineInbound helper against it:
node --import tsx scripts/proof-qa-lab-crabline-inbound.mts

# Supplemental focused regressions:
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/crabline-inbound-bounds.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/runtime-parity.test.ts --reporter=dot
```

### Evidence after fix

Real HTTP stall (production Crabline inbound helper against a live socket):

```text
[fetch-timeout] fetch timeout after 15000ms (elapsed 15001ms) operation=fetchWithSsrFGuard url=http://127.0.0.1:54050/stall
  ok: stalled inbound rejected (not hung) — elapsed=15046ms
  ok: bounded by the configured guarded-fetch deadline — elapsed=15046ms, budget=15000ms
  ok: unbounded inbound json() still hanging after 2000ms — state=still-hanging
  ok: completing inbound parsed message id — 42

ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS PASSED
```

### Observed result after fix

Against a real stalled admin-inbound socket, `postCrablineInbound` fails closed at ~15046ms — exactly the configured `QA_LAB_CRABLINE_INBOUND_TIMEOUT_MS` guarded-fetch deadline (`[fetch-timeout] fetch timeout after 15000ms`) — instead of hanging. The negative control — a raw `response.json()` on the same stalled socket — is still unresolved after a 2000ms observation window, confirming the pre-fix hang. A well-behaved completing body still parses to the telegram message id via the bounded reader.

### What was not tested

Live stall against a real Crabline admin-inbound or mock `/debug/requests` endpoint outside the harness.

### Fix classification

bugfix — timeout/hang

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted. Author reviewed the guarded-fetch timeout + bounded JSON wiring and caller-path proof output.
